skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render React/Remotion TSX components as MP4 videos through inference.sh with configurable duration, resolution, FPS, props, and codec.
skill.summary: Convert Remotion component code into rendered MP4 video files with configurable output settings.
skill.author: skillssh

security_audit.summary: The static Ruby backtick findings are Markdown formatting or examples, so they are false positives for direct shell execution. The skill still sends user TSX and props to inference.sh through infsh, and its broad infsh permission creates medium external service risk. No evidence found of prompt injection in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: User code and props are sent to an external renderer.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy notice and tell users not to include secrets, private code, or sensitive customer data.

remediation.issue: The allowed tool pattern permits any infsh command.
remediation.suggestion: Limit the permission to the specific render command if the host platform supports narrower Bash tool patterns.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation commands are shown in documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that related npx installation examples are optional and should only run after user approval.

static_findings.snippet: | `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |
| `composition_id` | string | No | Composition ID to render |
| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |
Your TSX code can import from `remotion` and `react`:
"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export
Render videos from React/Remotion component code via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

semantic_findings.title: External Rendering Service Receives User Code
semantic_findings.description: The skill sends user-provided Remotion TSX and props to inference.sh for remote rendering. This is expected behavior, but it creates privacy and external processing risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The description states that rendering uses inference.sh, and the examples pass TSX code through infsh app run. The behavior is explicit and central to the skill.

semantic_findings.title: Broad inference.sh CLI Permission
semantic_findings.description: The allowed tool pattern permits any infsh command. If future CLI subcommands expose sensitive actions, an agent could run more than the render command.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The front matter explicitly allows Bash(infsh *). The risk depends on available infsh subcommands, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.user_title: Render React Animations as MP4 Videos
content.value_statement: Teams need reliable videos from React animation code without manual export work. This skill sends Remotion TSX to inference.sh and returns an MP4 render.
actual_capabilities: Renders a default-exported Remotion React component into an MP4 file through inference.sh.
Accepts width, height, FPS, duration, codec, composition ID, and component props.
Supports common Remotion APIs such as useCurrentFrame, interpolate, spring, AbsoluteFill, Sequence, Audio, Video, and Img.
Provides CLI examples for title reveals, counters, spring motion, props, and sequence animations.
Shows Python SDK usage for standard runs and streaming progress updates.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, account login, and network access.
Uploads component code and props to an external rendering service.
Only imports available in the remote Remotion environment can run.
Render time, output URL availability, and errors depend on the remote service.

use_cases.title: Render motion prototypes
use_cases.description: Create MP4 previews from Remotion components for design review and social video experiments.

use_cases.title: Generate product videos
use_cases.description: Turn React animation components into repeatable launch videos, tutorials, or feature explainers.

use_cases.title: Export data explainers
use_cases.description: Render data-driven animations with props so charts and labels can change between exports.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic render
prompt_templates.prompt: Use remotion-render to create a three second MP4 title reveal at 1080p. Use simple Remotion code and return the video link.

prompt_templates.title: Add props and timing
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a square five second counter animation with props for title and target value. Use 60 FPS and concise styling.

prompt_templates.title: Build a data-driven animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 10 second data-driven motion graphic from this dataset. Use Remotion sequences, interpolation, and clear labels.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a production render
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a production render plan, then render after reviewing privacy risks. Set dimensions, FPS, duration, codec, props, and failure checks.

output_examples.input: A designer asks for a short fade-in launch title at 1920 by 1080.
output_examples.output: The skill returns an MP4 render link and confirms duration, FPS, and resolution.

output_examples.input: A developer provides a Remotion component with props for title and subtitle.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a rendered video link and notes that props were applied.

output_examples.input: A team requests progress updates for a ten second render.
output_examples.output: The skill reports render progress and then provides the final MP4 location.

best_practices: Review TSX code and props before sending them to inference.sh.
Keep assets, fonts, and imports available to the remote Remotion environment.
Start with short durations and lower resolution before production renders.
anti_patterns: Do not include secrets, tokens, private code, or customer data in render input.
Do not rely on local files that the remote renderer cannot access.
Do not run related installation commands unless the user asks for them.

faq.question: Does this skill render locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses inference.sh through the infsh CLI, so rendering happens outside the local workspace.

faq.question: What input does it need?
faq.answer: It needs a default-exported Remotion React component. Optional settings control props, dimensions, FPS, duration, composition ID, and codec.

faq.question: Can it use existing Remotion APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, interpolate, AbsoluteFill, Sequence, Audio, Video, and Img.

faq.question: Can I pass dynamic data?
faq.answer: Yes. Pass data through props, but remove secrets and sensitive records before rendering.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Install and authenticate the inference.sh CLI before using the skill.

faq.question: Is it safe for confidential projects?
faq.answer: Use caution. The render input is sent to an external service, so review policies before uploading private code or data.
